citations.quote:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at $0$ and at infinity, and the integral affine chart coordinate rings are $\mathbb Z[q]$ and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$.

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in P^+$. Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$, well defined by the highest-module presentation: its negative-half kernel is $\sum_iU_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}$, preserved by $\psi$ because every $F_i$ is fixed ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Equivalently the full highest-vector relations are bar stable: $E_i$ is fixed, the singular divided powers are fixed, and $\psi(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})=-q^{-\langle\lambda,h\rangle}K_{-h}(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})$. Hence the quotient involution is compatible with the algebra action and fixes $v_\lambda$. Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]); both are $\psi$-stable. Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=\mathcal L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$.

The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction on this page, whereas $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice $M_A$. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. The intersections $M_A\cap L$ and $M_A\cap L^-$ are respectively $\mathbb Z[q]$- and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-modules, generally not $A$-modules. The balanced part $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module; its Laurent extension $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$ is the full integral module once globalization is proved.

More generally a **based integrable module** $(M,B)$ here means exactly: $B$ is a homogeneous field basis; $M_A=\bigoplus_bAb$ is $U_A$-stable; the semilinear involution fixing $B$ is compatible with the algebra action; and $L_0=\bigoplus_bA_0b$ with residue $B$ is a crystal local basis at $0$. These are the four conditions of Lusztig 27.1.2(a)–(d) after the transport $v=q^{-1}$, together with the integrable extension used by Bao–Wang. Such data do not automatically imply an integral $\Theta$-action on an arbitrary based pair. A **based subobject** is a $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$; a **based quotient** is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send $B$ to the target basis or to $0$, and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral and bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.

The recursion of [[def-cyclotomic-polynomial]] is well posed: for every $n\ge1$
the division defining $\Phi_n$ is exact, $\Phi_n$ is a monic element of
$\mathbb Z[t]$,

$$\prod_{d\mid n}\Phi_d=t^{n}-1,$$

the product being over the positive divisors of $n$, and

$$\deg\Phi_n=\varphi(n)$$

([[def-unit-group-modulo-n-and-euler-totient]]). Moreover $(\Phi_n)_{n\ge1}$ is
the only family of monic polynomials in $\mathbb Z[t]$ satisfying the displayed
product identity for every $n\ge1$.

For every $n\ge1$ the cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_n$
([[def-cyclotomic-polynomial]]) is irreducible in $\mathbb Q[t]$
([[def-irreducible-and-prime-elements-in-a-domain]]).

The Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] is Noetherian, hence every ideal of
$\Lambda$ is finitely generated, and $\Lambda$ is a unique factorisation
domain; its units are $\pm t^k$, $k\in\mathbb Z$, and $t$ is prime in $\mathbb Z[t]$ but becomes a unit in $\Lambda$.

derivations.claim: **Cyclotomic denominators.** For $m=2\ell\ge6$, primitive $m$th roots occur in inverse pairs and none equals $1$ or $-1$. Thus $\Phi_m$ has even degree $2d$, integer coefficients, constant term $1$, and is reciprocal. Consequently $p=q^{-d}\Phi_m(q)$ belongs to $A$, is bar fixed, and is irreducible up to a unit in the unique-factorization ring $A$. Moreover $1/p=q^d/\Phi_m(q)$ is regular at zero with strictly positive valuation; bar invariance gives strictly positive valuation at infinity in the parameter $q^{-1}$. Different values of $\ell$ give nonassociate irreducibles. Finally $p$ divides $[\ell]_q$, since a primitive $2\ell$th root is a simple zero of $q^\ell-q^{-\ell}$ and not a zero of $q-q^{-1}$.

**The needed Gaussian congruences.** Put $z=q^2$ and reduce modulo $\Phi_{2\ell}(q)$, so $z$ is a primitive $\ell$th root and $q^\ell=-1$. The finite identity $\prod_{h=0}^{N-1}(1+z^hX)=\sum_{k=0}^N z^{k(k-1)/2}\binom{N}{k}_zX^k$, proved by multiplying one factor at a time, and the block identity $\prod_{h=0}^{\ell-1}(1+z^hX)=1-(-X)^\ell$ give the Gaussian digit rule: a coefficient with lower remainder exceeding upper remainder modulo $\ell$ vanishes; when the remainders agree, the remaining coefficient comes from the ordinary binomial expansion of the full blocks. Since $\binom{N}{k}_q=q^{-k(N-k)}\binom{N}{k}_{q^2}$, for $r=\ell-1$ this gives $\binom{r+k}{k}_q=0\bmod p$ unless $k=t\ell$, and gives $\binom{r+t\ell}{t\ell}_q=(-1)^{t(\ell-1)}\bmod p$. Indeed the lower remainder is nonzero exactly in the vanishing cases, while in the other cases the unsymmetrized coefficient is $1$ and the symmetrizing factor is $q^{-t\ell(\ell-1)}=(-1)^{t(\ell-1)}$. The argument takes place in the integral domain $A/(p)$ and proves divisibility in $A$, rather than merely pointwise numerical vanishing.

**Modular divided-power homomorphisms.** Fix $j$, write $\ell=\ell_j$, $n=j\ell$, $r=\ell-1$ and $m=n+2r=n_{j+1}$. In $V_A(m)/(p_j)$, the vector $v=u_{j+1,r}$ has weight $n$. For $1\le a\le r$, the coefficient of $E^{(a)}v$ is $\binom{m-r+a}{a}_q=\binom{(j+1)\ell-1+a}{a}_q$, whose upper remainder $a-1$ is smaller than the lower remainder $a$; hence it is zero by step 2.1. For $a>r$ the action is already zero. Also $F^{(k)}v=\binom{r+k}{k}_q u_{j+1,r+k}$ vanishes modulo $p_j$ whenever $k>n$: until $k=(j+1)\ell-1$ its remainder is nonzero, and for $k\ge(j+1)\ell$ the target position exceeds $m$. Therefore $u_{j,k}\mapsto F^{(k)}v$ defines a homomorphism of the complete divided strings modulo $p_j$. To check all generators, divided $F$ compatibility is the Gaussian product identity for $F^{(a)}F^{(k)}$; divided $E$ compatibility follows by reordering $E^{(a)}F^{(k)}$ and using the just-proved annihilation of all positive divided $E$ powers on the weight-$n$ vector $v$, leaving exactly $\binom{n-k+a}{a}_q F^{(k-a)}v$; the vanished positions $k>n$ respect the source endpoints. Every toral generator and toral quantum binomial has the same weight scalar on matched positions. Step 2.1 identifies this homomorphism with $T_j$ modulo $p_j$, so $(aT_j-T_ja)V_A(n_j)\subseteq p_j V_A(n_{j+1})$ for every $a\in U_A$.

**Exact vanishing of consecutive shears.** The nonzero target positions of $T_j$ are $k=r_j+t\ell_j=(t+1)\ell_j-1$, $0\le t\le j$. Reduced modulo $\ell_{j+1}=\ell_j+1$, their residues are $\ell_j-t-1$, ranging from $2$ to $\ell_j-1$. None is zero. Since $T_{j+1}$ is supported precisely on positions divisible by $\ell_{j+1}$, one has $T_{j+1}T_j=0$ exactly. Other products $T_iT_j$ vanish because their source and target summands do not match. On every vector only finitely many $T_j$ act, so $S$ is algebraic, $S^2=0$, and $C^{-1}=1-S$. The equality $n_{j+1}=n_j+2r_j$ also shows each $T_j$ preserves weights.

**Integral action, including the cross terms.** Put $L_A=\bigoplus_j V_A(n_j)$. For $a\in U_A$, the standard action preserves each summand of $L_A$, and $C^{-1}aC=a+[a,S]-SaS$ by step 4.1. Step 3.1 makes every column of $[a,T_j]/p_j$ integral. The only potentially nonzero summands of $SaS$ are $T_{j+1}aT_j/(p_{j+1}p_j)$. The numerator is divisible by $p_j$, because it equals $T_{j+1}(aT_j-T_ja)$ using $T_{j+1}T_j=0$; it is divisible by $p_{j+1}$, because it also equals $(T_{j+1}a-aT_{j+1})T_j$. These are entrywise divisibilities of matrices in standard divided bases. The distinct irreducibles $p_j,p_{j+1}$ are coprime in the unique-factorization ring $A$, so their product divides every entry. Thus all cross terms are integral. For every input column there are at most two shear positions, so all sums remain finite. It follows that $C^{-1}aC$ preserves $L_A$, equivalently $aM_A\subseteq M_A$. This checks the full divided-power integral form, not just $E$ and $F$.

**The basis and its compatible bar.** The inverse from step 4.1 makes $B=C\{u_{j,k}\}$ a field basis and makes its $A$-span free with that basis. Homogeneity was checked there. Each coefficient $(-1)^{t(\ell_j-1)}/p_j$ is bar fixed by step 1.1, so the standard module bar fixes each $b_{j,k}$; consequently this is exactly the basis-fixing bar of $B$ and retains its compatibility with the $U$ action. Every vector has finitely many summand components, each in a finite divided string, so $E,F$ are locally nilpotent, the chosen weight grading is a direct sum, and $M$ is integrable. No arbitrary selection of vectors or bases is used.

**Crystal charts and balancedness.** Let $L_0$ and $L_\infty$ be the standard direct-sum regular charts. Step 1.1 shows that both $C$ and $C^{-1}$ preserve these charts and are the identity on their zero and infinity residues: their nonidentity entries are signed $1/p_j$, in $qA_0$ and $q^{-1}A_\infty$, respectively. Therefore the $B$-generated regular charts equal the standard ones, and the residues of $B$ equal the standard divided-string crystal vertices. Kashiwara stability and the crystal inverse relations follow directly from [F1], so the fourth based axiom holds. In the common basis $B$, the integral lattice and charts have coefficient rings $A,A_0,A_\infty$. Their simultaneous intersection has integer coefficients because a Laurent polynomial regular at both zero and infinity is an integer constant. Also $A\cap A_0=\mathbb Z[q]$. Hence the integral balanced map is the coefficientwise isomorphism $\bigoplus_B\mathbb Z\longrightarrow\bigoplus_B\mathbb Z[q]/q\mathbb Z[q]$. All coefficient families have finite support.

**The explicit top action and conclusion.** Since $u_{j,0}$ is highest, $E^{(r_j)}u_{j,0}=0$. Also $b_{j,0}=u_{j,0}+u_{j+1,r_j}/p_j$, so [F1] gives $E^{(r_j)}b_{j,0}=(G_j/p_j)u_{j+1,0}$. Replacing $u_{j+1,0}$ by $b_{j+1,0}-u_{j+2,r_{j+1}}/p_{j+1}$ gives the stated formula, because $r_{j+1}=j+3$ is not divisible by $\ell_{j+2}=j+5$ and thus $u_{j+2,r_{j+1}}=b_{j+2,r_{j+1}}$. Gaussian polynomials are nonzero in $K$, so $G_j\ne0$; step 5.1 proves that both coefficients are in $A$. Steps 4.1–7.1 establish every claimed basis, action, bar, integrability, crystal and balanced property for this actual algebraic module.
